## My Thinking

My family has farmed this land for generations. Everyone around here in Quzhou grows winter wheat then summer maize — two crops on the same land every year. That's just what you do on the North China Plain. The grain station buys both. I know prices are never great but I know what I know, and I can't afford to gamble on something unfamiliar.

I have about 10 mu of flat, decent loamy soil. My well still reaches water, though the neighbors say it's getting harder every year. Doesn't matter — I need it for wheat especially in spring.

For wheat, I plow in October after the machines come through from the county cooperative. I'll buy the same improved seed variety I used last two years — the local agri-supply store stocks Jimai 22, works well enough. I put down base fertilizer before sowing — compound fertilizer plus extra urea — then top-dress at jointing. I water three times: the winter irrigation before the ground freezes, once at jointing, once when heads are forming. Two sprays for aphids and mildew, that's normal.

Once wheat is off in June, I seed maize straight into the stubble without plowing — saves me money and time, and the neighbors have been doing it that way the last few years. Hybrid seed, the dealer always has Xianyu 335. Maize mostly gets summer rain so I only pump once, at silking if it's dry. One pesticide spray for corn borer.

I don't experiment. I do what my father did, adjusted a little by what neighbors say worked last year.
